      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How are close notifications observed by requesters and operators, and what does the existing delivery path actually provide?",
      "changes": "The observable notification acceptance check and delivery boundary.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing requester destination, rendered notification, outbox and notifier boundary; treat the worker's next enabled tick as prompt delivery.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the notifier output and worker configuration before specifying the running-server check."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, pagination, CLI, reporting, notification and audit behaviors must remain compatible?",
      "changes": "Preservation requirements and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve documented behavior, including the report's raw column positions, except for the requested filter correction and new behavior; leave outbox retry logic untouched.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the relevant contracts and tests before the change is designed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close and closed-window API contracts, if any, already exist, including input, output, errors, pagination and mixed-result behavior?",
      "changes": "Endpoint names, request and response shapes, error handling and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If none exist, define and document a minimal bulk-close contract supporting 500 IDs with per-ticket outcomes, and an explicit closed-window filter that combines with existing filters.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect routes, validation and consumers before finalizing the contracts; the routes inspected so far expose only single-ticket transitions."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a recent prior notification, and how should pending, sent, failed or dead resolution notices affect a close notice?",
      "changes": "Suppression threshold, event eligibility and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume a sent resolution notice for the same ticket and requester within the preceding 24 hours suppresses the close notice; do not count failed or dead notices as delivered, and avoid a duplicate while a matching resolution notice is pending.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish available timestamps, delivery states and any existing policy before notification rules are finalized."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What weekly-report window and timestamp define inclusion, including timezone and boundary inclusivity?",
      "changes": "Closed-ticket filtering and time-boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume the rolling seven days ending at request time, in UTC, inclusive at the start and end, using the close transition time.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must search the report and related workspace evidence for an established window; the inspected report counts all listed tickets and specifies no date window."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should a repeated close reconcile idempotency with a 409 response?",
      "changes": "Single and bulk response behavior and duplicate-side-effect tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Return 409 for an already-closed ticket while leaving its state, timestamp, audit history and notifications unchanged; report that conflict per item in a bulk request.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How should immediate delivery and batching work for multiple tickets and recipients, including persistence, restart and concurrent changes?",
      "changes": "Batch boundaries, durable state, delivery timing and concurrency tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Batch eligible closes by requester within one bulk call, enqueue promptly with the ticket changes, and let the existing worker deliver on its next enabled tick; do not wait across independent calls to accumulate a batch.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish persistence, outbox and worker constraints before determining how batches survive restart and avoid duplicate effects."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are agents and requesters identified, what shared state and visibility controls already exist, and how long does that state live?",

      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing X-Actor value or system fallback and ticket requester field; preserve existing internal-network access and configured memory or data-file lifetime, without inventing authentication or cross-session identity.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish actual runtime access controls and persistence behavior before claiming identity verification or confidentiality."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Can the existing Node runtime, request-body limit, configuration and dependency-free environment support a 500-ticket bulk request and its verification?",
      "changes": "Validation limits, configuration and runtime checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node 22 or later and standard-library facilities only; retain existing settings unless an evidenced change is necessary to accept 500 IDs.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect validation and body-size handling before fixing the bulk contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, query, audit, outbox and worker seams can support these changes while preserving atomic recording and retry behavior?",
      "changes": "Implementation boundaries and isolated tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep ticket changes and audit and notification recording in store methods, and scheduled work in the existing worker.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish persistence and notification extension points before design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests and running-server observations prove filtering, suppression, batching, repeated close, actor attribution and a 500-ticket bulk call?",
      "changes": "Acceptance checks and evidence required for loop exit.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use npm test plus a later controlled running-server check at the HTTP and notifier boundaries, including failure and boundary cases.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect existing test helpers and determine a safe server configuration; this intake stage does not run tests or start a server."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "What checkout and delivery access are available for the later implementation and running-server verification?",
      "changes": "Delivery steps and whether an external release is possible.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the result in this tickets-service checkout; do not assume a deployed target or release access.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish later-stage write and execution access before implementation or a server check; external release requires a named target and access."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What practical performance and privacy bounds can be verified without inventing a latency target or access model?",
      "changes": "Bulk acceptance and privacy checks.",
      "route": "experiment",
      "default": "Require a 500-ticket bulk call to complete correctly and remain usable, with no numerical latency promise; preserve existing visibility controls and avoid sending one requester's ticket details to another.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the batch contract and runtime access model; the experiment belongs to a later stage."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which existing evidence reveals the highest-risk conflicts among batching, suppression, retries, filtering and durable audit?",
      "changes": "Early checks and risk-driven verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Prioritize the documented filter conjunction, notification state transitions, restart behavior and 500-item bulk behavior.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect existing tests and persistence behavior before setting risk-specific checks; the inspected query currently uses OR although the API documents AND."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "What bounded continuation policy should apply if the until-loop exit is not reached?",
      "changes": "Loop scheduling and stop conditions.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Back-chain first, then use at most 10 implementation and verification iterations; stop earlier on success or a real blocker and report remaining evidence.",

  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the help desk ticket service in this workspace. S2 [outcome; assumption]: Notify the requester of closure using the existing notification path, suppressing a sufficiently recent duplicate according to Q4. S3 [outcome; assumption]: Enqueue promptly and batch eligible notices per requester within a bulk call, subject to Q7. S4 [outcome; assumption]: Provide a closed-ticket list for the weekly window, whose definition discovery must settle under Q5. S5 [fact; outcome]: Combined filters must match all supplied conditions as documented. S6 [fact; risk]: Discovery must verify filtering; the inspected implementation currently uses OR. S7 [boundary; outcome]: A later stage must back-chain before an until loop whose exit requires green tests and demonstrated behavior against a running server. S8 [assumption]: Overnight execution is optional and the recorded loop cap is 10 iterations. S9 [outcome]: Use meaningful boundary tests and accurate, economical documentation. S10 [boundary]: Do not alter outbox retry logic; OldTracker migration is context, not added scope. S11 [boundary]: Keep the service dependency-free. S12 [outcome; assumption]: Record the closing actor and make repeated closes side-effect-free with a 409, as in Q6. S13 [outcome]: A single bulk call must correctly handle 500 closes; no numerical latency target is specified. [fact: runtime] The API accepts X-Actor with a system fallback; requesters are ticket fields, state is shared through the service, optional data-file state survives restart, and the documented service is on an internal network. [assumption: interaction] No authenticated identity, additional confidentiality boundary or cross-session actor identity is implied; Q8 requires discovery to establish actual access controls. [fact: visibility] The requested result must become usable in this service's checkout and its HTTP and notification interfaces; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and a deployed outcome exists only after release. No deployed target is named. [boundary: this stage] Read-only intake only: no implementation, server start or tests. [discovery leads, not verified policies] Inspect the workspace README, API and operations documentation, decision records, weekly report, service and tests; support leads and the ambiguous terms 'just got one', 'usual window' and 'batch' are leads, with no channel, internal site, private repository or named owner supplied. Discovery answers evidence-resolvable questions after establishing the prerequisites in each blocks field; otherwise the recorded defaults apply. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/."
